newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan gives UK firm $7.6 mln bridge supply deal.
newsitem.headline: Sudan gives UK firm $7.6 mln bridge supply deal.

text.p: Sudan has signed a $7.6 million contract for British firm Balfour Kilpatrick to supply raw materials to build four bridges, a Khartoum weekly said on Sunday.

The firm is a unit of cable and construction firm BICC Plc and the bridges are part of the 1,205 km (750 mile) Western Salvation Highway which will run southwards from Khartoum and also connect Sudan with its neighbour Chad.
The New Horizon weekly did not say when the contract was signed but added that Ramsis Engineering Co. would construct the bridges, expected to be finished within three months.
The cost of the highway is estimated at $120 million and the daily said that most of the funds would be contributions by the six states in the Kordofan and Darfur provinces of Sudan.
The newspaper said that workers at the ministry of roads and communications pledged they would donate more than $17,000 from their salaries for the project.
Sudanese Minister of Roads and Communications al-Hadi Bushra was quoted by the paper as saying he was happy that the supply contract was awarded to a British firm.

There are very few foreign companies working in Sudan due to instability sparked by rebel offensives, economic difficulties and charges that the government of Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir violates human rights.
